metadata.title: The sharp $L^2$-Michael--Simon inequality
metadata.abstract: Let $n \geq 3$. We prove that if $j \colon (\Sigma^n,g) \to (\mathbb{R}^N,dx^2)$ is an isometric immersion, then \begin{equation*} \int_\Sigma \left( \lvert \nabla u \rvert^2 + \frac{n(n-2)}{4}\lvert H \rvert^2 u^2 \right) \geq \frac{n(n-2)}{4}\mathrm{Vol}(S^n)^{2/n}\left( \int_\Sigma \lvert u \rvert^{\frac{2n}{n-2}} \right)^{\frac{n-2}{n}} \end{equation*} for all $u \in W^{1,2}(\Sigma)$, and characterize immersions for which equality is realized. Our proof exploits the conformal invariance of the inequality, and hence extends to sharp Michael--Simon inequalities for submanifolds of the sphere, of hyperbolic space, and of other conformally developable manifolds. As an application, we derive Chen--Fenchel--Willmore-type inequalities relating $L^p$-norms of the mean curvature vector to the volume of a compact submanifold of a simply-connected spaceform.
